The second operation derives its row only from the newly inserted response. Claim/response uniqueness failure rolls back the whole batch; the catch only rereads a winner for a UNIQUE-constraint error and verifies both client-key and normalized-payload digests. Other storage failures propagate. Actual D1 tests prove eight simultaneous identical requests commit one response, competing keys/payloads produce one winner, and a forced claim failure leaves no orphan response.
